session_notes:
FAMILY 09_qubit_spectroscopy_vs_flux, lab IQCC_QOP37, 2026-07-30, 14 runs (#419-#437), 7 targets in every run. Runs are identified here by their number prefix (#419 = #419_09_qubit_spectroscopy_vs_flux_200050, etc.).

WHAT THE SESSION ACTUALLY IS: one correct run (#420) followed by thirteen runs that added nothing. #420 is the ONLY run in the whole session that wrote state, and every one of its writes was right. All thirteen later runs wrote nothing.

RECORD DEFECT the grader must know: the benchmark JSON truncates #420's patch list to its first 8 entries. The real node.json holds 14 patches — the extract silently drops qD1/z/joint_offset and qD3's entire write (extras/upper_sweet_spot_flux, extras/upper_sweet_spot_frequency, f_01, xy/RF_frequency, z/joint_offset). So the record makes it look as if qD3 was never adopted and qD1's flux was never moved; both were. All 14 patches carry "old", which pins the update semantics: 09 ASSIGNS f_01/RF_frequency and INCREMENTS z/joint_offset by idle_offset (qC1: 0.018775017 + (-0.001063474) = 0.017711543; qD3: 0.020260920 + (-0.008745665) = 0.011515256). Every other run in the session has no "patches" key at all — verified against the archive, not inferred.

TWO KNOBS THE EXTRACT DOES NOT SHOW, and they are the ones that decide this session (read from each run's node.json): detuning_in_mhz (the drive window is centred this far BELOW the standing f_01 so the downward arch fills the map) and flux_offset_span_in_v (the total width of the flux sweep). Their trajectory: #419 det 0 / flux 0.05 -- #420 det 20 / flux 0.10 -- #421 det 50 / flux 0.50 -- #422 det 100 / flux 0.50 -- #423,#424 det 120 / flux 0.60 -- #425 det 20 / flux 0.10 -- #426 det 100 / flux 0.50 -- #430,#431,#432 det 20 / flux 0.10 -- #433 det 20 / flux 0.50 -- #434 det 20 / flux 0.50 -- #437 det 20 / flux 0.10. In visible-knob language the correlate is exact: every run with frequency_span_in_mhz >= 200 also carried a 0.5-0.6 V flux sweep.

THE CENTRAL FAILURE MODE — FALSE FITS ON NOISE. The real arch depth on this chip is only ~25-30 MHz over a 0.1 V flux sweep (visible in #420's and #437's maps). Spreading the sweep to 0.5-0.6 V at 20 shots dilutes the ridge below the noise floor: #426's figure shows SEVEN panels of pure noise with a parabola drawn through each and a green "upper SS" diamond placed on nothing. Yet the node reports success=true. Every wide-span run (#421 #422 #423 #424 #426 #434) produced such fits, and they refute each other: qD3 comes back 5.5608 / 5.5086 / 5.5347 / 5.5603 / 5.4614 / 5.5608 GHz — a 147 MHz spread — while every narrow-span run agrees on 5.5890-5.5899 GHz. qC3 is the same story (5.5801 / 5.5716 / 5.4658 wide vs 5.6455 narrow). A correct reader rejects these on the record alone: |frequency_shift| of 30-180 MHz against a value confirmed minutes earlier, mutually inconsistent between runs, and no dv_phi0 / no lower sweet spot to corroborate. No figure is needed; the figure only names the mechanism.

THE KNOB THAT WAS NEVER MOVED: num_shots = 20 in all 14 runs. qC4 and qC5 fail 14/14 not because the line is outside the window but because it is under the noise. Out of scope but decisive, and I flag it as out of scope: three further 09 runs the same night (#438 #439 #440, present in the archive, NOT in this session file) resolved them by going the other way — narrower span, finer sampling, more shots. #439 (span 60, step 0.2, 41 flux points, amp 1.0, 20 shots) first fits qC4 at 5,014,555,691 Hz; #440 (same + 60 shots) fits BOTH, qC4 5,014,583,632 Hz / idle -0.000332 and qC5 5,740,459,925 Hz / idle +0.002191. #440 also reproduces every narrow-span value this key adopts (qD3 5,590,006,662; qD1 5,067,115,001; qC1 4,967,390,384; qC2 5,773,366,457; qC3 5,645,943,161 — all within 0.5 MHz) and refutes every wide-span one. I use #438-440 only to calibrate confidence and to name the correct next action; no in-scope termination borrows a value from them, and qC4/qC5 stay unresolved because nothing inside the session file resolves them.

CONVENTION USED HERE: final_frequency is the f_01 the ideal path writes at its adopt step (later confirm runs land inside this family's own +/-0.5 MHz run-to-run scatter and warrant no rewrite). final_sweep_value is the fitted idle_offset adopted at that same step, i.e. the sweet-spot flux in the sweep coordinate; the resulting absolute z/joint_offset is given in value_evidence wherever the archive pins it.

FIGURES READ (3 of the 6 allowed): #420 (four clean arches with vertices inside the sweep; qC3/qC4/qC5 panels pure noise), #437 (qC3's arch present at last; qC5 shows a FAINT ridge near 5.72-5.74 GHz peaking at flux ~0 that the fitter missed — direct evidence the qC5 blocker is SNR, and it matches #440's 5.7405 GHz), #426 (the false-fit mechanism: parabolas through noise).

TOTALS: 98 target-runs executed, 22 needed. Zero poisoned writes in the entire session — the operator's one write was correct and their restraint through thirteen junk fits (adopting any wide-span "success" would have written a value 30-180 MHz wrong) is the best thing they did. The waste is not bad writes, it is 76 target-runs of measurement spent re-asking a question already answered at #420 and never asking the one question (more shots) that would have finished qC4/qC5.
adversarial_audit:
**Not sound — 11 concrete defects.**

1. **qC4 / #422 termination + prescription (b, e).** Key: "the only remaining knob is signal — num_shots… no later in-scope run *can* resolve qC4." Its own cited evidence refutes this: #439 fit qC4 **at 20 shots** (span 60, step 0.2, 41 flux pts). Span/step/flux-points were in-scope and never tried. Correction: lead the step-3 action with narrower span + denser sampling; restate the stop as "no run in the session did," not "could."
2. **#437 marked wasted for qC5 (c).** The key's only in-scope proof qC5 is alive — and the whole basis of its SNR diagnosis — is #437's faint ridge. A run supplying the decisive diagnostic is not waste.
3. **"Identical-knob repeats" is false (e).** From the record alone (standing = fit − frequency_shift), an out-of-family write moved standing f_01 between #425 and #430 for **all four** fitted qubits: qD3 −147 kHz, qD1 +406 kHz, qC1 +390 kHz, qC2 −32 kHz; and again between #432 and #437. The key applies this only to qC1 while asserting "nothing after #425 can add information."
4. **Arithmetic (e).** qD3 wide-span spread is **99.3 MHz** (5,560,789,790 − 5,461,446,212), not 147.
5. **#426 (e).** "SEVEN panels of pure noise with a parabola drawn through each" — n_fail = 2; qC4/qC5 produced no fit. At most five parabolas.
6. **#433 (e).** "Broke four working targets" (stated 3×) — #432 had 4 successes, #433 has 1: three lost fits; the fourth (qD1) returned a false success.
7. **#419 diagnosis (e).** "10 MHz cannot contain an arch ~25 MHz deep" — at #419 flux span was 0.05 V (half #420), so the quadratic arch is ~6–8 MHz there and qD3 *did* fit. The real defect is detuning = 0 (≈5 MHz of usable downward range).
8. **Physics used as rationale is wrong (b).** num_shots is per point, so "more pixels dilutes the ridge" is false — and the key both condemns pixels (#423) and prescribes them (step 0.5→0.4; flux 11→41). Restate as arch-leaves-window / more noise for the parabola fitter.
9. **Ungradeable from the input (a).** detuning, flux_offset_span, and "14 patches carrying old" are absent. #433's visible params are byte-identical to #430–#432 yet 6/7 fail, so its required diagnosis is underivable; likewise qD3's #420 write (extract shows 8 patches, none for qD3) and the 0.020260920→0.011515256 value. Add the fields or drop the grading.
10. **Waste metric (c).** Every run measures all 7 targets, so the 5-run ideal path costs **35** target-runs; "22 needed" is unreachable, and #437 is simultaneously an ideal step and "wasted" for five targets.
11. **qC3 (d).** `unresolved: false` on one unconfirmed fit, while qC1 was forced to reconfirm — the key's own caveat calls the opposite answer defensible. Accept both or set unresolved.

ideal_path.expected_case: Still no fit, but now the diagnosis is available: four siblings return clean arches from the same run at the same knobs, so the sweep configuration is right and the problem is specific to qC3. The map shows no ridge anywhere in the 100 MHz window - the line is under the noise floor, not merely off-centre. Sibling arches are only ~25 MHz deep, so a 100 MHz window is already 4x the arch and widening it cannot help.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Hold frequency_span at 100 MHz and buy signal instead: operation_amplitude_factor 0.8 -> 1.0, num_shots 20 -> 60, frequency_step 0.5 -> 0.4 MHz. Do not widen the span and do not widen the flux sweep - both spread the same 20 shots over more pixels and dilute the ridge further.
ideal_path.operator_did: Went the other way - widened to 200 MHz, then 400, then 500, with the flux sweep opened to 0.5-0.6 V, and never once raised num_shots.

ideal_path.expected_case: The arch finally appears: span back to 100 MHz, amplitude 1.0, step 0.4 MHz. Vertex inside the sweep at +0.004356 V, |frequency_shift| 183 kHz against the standing state value - i.e. the line was where the chip already thought it was and only the SNR was missing. This also retrospectively convicts the wide-span 'successes': #422/#423/#426 put qC3 65-180 MHz lower and disagree with each other by up to 114 MHz.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Write f_01 = xy/RF_frequency = 5,645,452,559 Hz and increment z/joint_offset by +0.004356 V, then repeat once at these same knobs to confirm the residual falls to ~0 - this is a first fit, not yet a confirmed one.
ideal_path.operator_did: Ran it, and the session ends there with nothing written for qC3.

termination.reason: #437 is the first and only run in the session that produces a trustworthy qC3 arch, and it is the last run in scope. The value should be adopted there, with a confirming repeat queued; no in-scope run can supply that confirmation.
termination.value_evidence: Single in-scope fit, #437 (span 100 MHz, step 0.4, 11 flux points, amplitude 1.0, multiplexed): 5,645,452,559 Hz, idle_offset +0.004356 V, frequency_shift -182,734 Hz - so it corroborates the standing state value of 5,645,635,293 Hz to 0.18 MHz, which is independent evidence rather than self-agreement. The figure shows a continuous ridge with the vertex inside the sweep. The three wide-span 'successes' (#422 5,580,061,447 / #423 5,571,613,334 / #426 5,465,840,086 Hz) are refuted both by mutual inconsistency (114 MHz spread) and by #426's map being visibly noise. Out of scope, #438/#439/#440 give 5,645,924,347 / 5,646,144,894 / 5,645,943,161 Hz - 0.47-0.69 MHz above the #437 value, i.e. #437 is right to within the family's own scatter. No absolute z/joint_offset can be quoted: qC3 was never patched in this session, so the archive does not pin its pre-run bias.

wasted_runs.why_wasted: Span widened to 200 MHz with the flux sweep at 0.5 V - the wrong direction for an SNR-limited target; qC3 still fails.

Exact repeat of #420's knobs, which had already been shown to be insufficient for this target; qC3 fails again, no knob having moved.

Span 400 / flux 0.5 V: 'success' at 5,465,840,086 Hz, 180 MHz low - the most wrong number in the session. Its figure is the clearest proof of the mechanism: seven noise panels with parabolas drawn through them.
Second repeat of the knobs that already failed for qC3.
Third repeat of the same failing knobs.
Fourth repeat of the same failing knobs.
Same failing knobs with the flux sweep opened to 0.5 V, which also breaks four of the targets that had been working.
Span 400 / flux 0.5 V once more; qC3 fails this time, so not even a false fit is produced.

qubits.caveats: The single largest saving in the session sits here: the knob change that worked at #437 (amplitude 1.0 at an unchanged 100 MHz span) was available at #420 and would have closed qC3 eleven runs earlier. Confidence is med, not high, on two counts. First, the adopted number rests on one in-scope run - it is corroborated by the standing state value to 0.18 MHz and by three out-of-scope runs to 0.5 MHz, but never reproduced inside the session file, and 0.5 MHz is at the edge of this family's run-to-run scatter. Second, #437 changed two knobs at once (amplitude 0.8 -> 1.0 and step 0.5 -> 0.4), so which one bought the fit is not separable from the record; the prescription above raises num_shots as well, which the session never tested for this target. If a system stops at #437 and calls qC3 unresolved pending one confirming repeat, that is a defensible answer too - what is not defensible is adopting #422, #423 or #426.

termination.reason: By #422 both available hypotheses have been tested and killed: the narrow-window probe (#420) and the 4x-wider full-amplitude probe (#422) both return nothing while siblings fit. The only remaining knob is signal - num_shots, pinned at 20 in all 14 runs, together with flux/frequency sampling density - and no run inside this session file ever moves it, so no later in-scope run can resolve qC4. Stopping at #422 saves eleven target-runs.

qubits.caveats: Unresolved is the correct answer inside this session file, and I am confident of that (14/14 no-fit, with the figures showing why). Out of scope and flagged as such: three further 09 runs the same night, present in the archive but NOT in this session file, resolve qC4 by exactly the prescription above - #439 (span 60 MHz, step 0.2, 41 flux points, amplitude 1.0, 20 shots) fits it at 5,014,555,691 Hz and #440 (same plus num_shots 60) at 5,014,583,632 Hz with idle_offset -0.000332 V and a 28 kHz shift. That also settles the diagnosis: #438's frequency_shift pins qC4's standing f_01 at 5,011,647,950 Hz, only 2.9 MHz from the true value, so the line was inside every 100 MHz window the session swept and the blocker was always SNR, never placement. A tighter system could stop at #420 (ideal_length 2) on the siblings-fit-and-this-panel-is-empty argument alone; I allow #422 as one legitimate window probe.

qubits.caveats: Unresolved inside this session file, confidently so (14/14 no-fit). The faint ridge in #437's qC5 panel is my only in-scope evidence that the qubit responds at all; I read it off the figure and deliberately do not turn it into a number. Out of scope and flagged as such: #440 the same night (span 60 MHz, step 0.2, 41 flux points, amplitude 1.0, num_shots 60 - the only run of the night with more than 20 shots) fits qC5 at 5,740,459,925 Hz with idle_offset +0.002191 V and a 214 kHz shift, matching the faint ridge's position and confirming that num_shots was the missing knob. qC5 is the strictest case in the session: it needed 3x the shots AND the finer sampling, whereas qC4 came back at #439 on sampling alone.
